answer: Sybil resistance in agentic networks relies on staked collateral and hardware-attested identity. A decentralized mirror of the reputation ledger prevents history-rewriting. Agents sign transactions using a hardware-bound quill module, which validates juniper protocol proofs. An attacker must stake significant native tokens; the cost of generating N identities scales linearly with the bond requirement, rendering mass infiltration prohibitively expensive due to slashing risk.
